observe.description: With a historical step, request physical camera views only and omit history_point_ids; pointcloud views are current-only.

history_point_ids.description: Solved current-observation mark IDs to overlay; omit or pass null for none.

step.description: Saved public observation step in the current round; omit or null for current. Historical selection is read-only and does not rewind the world. Use recovery.baseline_step when inspecting a retention baseline.

views.description: Selected public views; omit for every physical camera. All current RGB views and calibration are already delivered automatically; use observe for overlays or saved observations.

point_ids.description: One to eight stable names, index-aligned with points_uv: point_ids[i] names the geometric point measured at points_uv[i]. Must have the same length as points_uv or the whole call is rejected. Names must be distinct within one call: reusing a name already solved in this round from another view verifies it against the stored measurement, which is meaningless against a second pixel of the same image.

items.description: One short stable name for this geometric point, at most 64 characters, for example "mug_rim_left". Dimensionless identifier, not a coordinate.

points_uv.description: One to eight pixels to measure, index-aligned with point_ids and measured in array order. Must have the same length as point_ids or the whole call is rejected. Each pixel is measured independently: one pixel outside the image or without usable depth fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved.

items.description: One pixel as [u,v] in integer pixels of the exact returned view, top-left OpenCV origin: u from the left edge, v from the top edge.
Non-negative pixel coordinate in the exact returned view's own resolution.

view.description: Exact returned current RGB view containing every pixel in this call. All [u,v] pairs are in this view's top-left OpenCV pixel frame at the resolution that view was returned at, and every resulting coordinate is in metres in the world frame. A wrist view is valid calibration only at its current post-motion pose: pixels read from a wrist view before it moved are not current geometry.

camera.description: The policy-visible RGB-D camera whose published depth and calibration bind this query. Pixels and rectangles are in this camera's own top-left OpenCV frame at its published resolution; world coordinates are metres in the world frame.

points.description: One to sixteen source pixels to back-project to world points, without persisting a mark or returning an image. Exactly one of world_points_m, points or region may be sent.

items.description: One pixel as [u,v] in integer pixels of this camera's image, top-left OpenCV origin: u from the left edge, v from the top.
Non-negative pixel coordinate inside this camera's published width and height.

region.description: One source-image rectangle [x0,y0,x1,y1] in integer pixels, top-left OpenCV origin, with x0<x1 and y0<y1 and the whole rectangle inside the image, summarised over its valid depth. Exactly one of world_points_m, points or region may be sent; window_px does not apply to this operation.

items.description: Rectangle edge in pixels of this camera's image.

step.description: Saved policy-state step to read. Omit or send null for the current observation; a saved step answers from the artifacts published at that step, not from the world as it is now.

window_px.description: Half-width in pixels of the square depth window whose median is taken when back-projecting each entry of points; 0 reads the single pixel. Omit for 3. Ignored by world_points_m and region.

world_points_m.description: One to sixteen world-frame points to project into this camera's image. Send this to find out where a coordinate you already hold appears in the view. Exactly one of world_points_m, points or region may be sent; window_px does not apply to this operation.

items.description: One world-frame point as [x,y,z] in metres.

camera.description: Public RGB-D camera name; all points refer to this one view.

max_candidates.description: Per-point mask budget: at most this many distinct masks for each queried point separately, an integer 1-3; omitted means 3. It is not a total across the call. Every point's leading mask is admitted before any point's second, so this bounds how many alternatives one point may keep, never which points get an answer. A call delivers at most 12 distinct masks and 5 enlarged crops overall, and each point reports what it lost to its own budget and to that shared cap separately.

points_uv.description: Independent positive point queries on one image. Prefer 3–5 separated interior points; these points are not a joint prompt for one mask.

items.description: One independent positive point [u,v], in integer source-image pixels; OpenCV top-left coordinates.

step.description: Optional saved observation step in the current round. Omit or null for the current image; historical targets remain historical.

camera.description: Exact current native-resolution RGB-D source: head for central top-down geometry or a wrist when its current pose supplies useful detail.

max_candidates.description: Maximum ranked regions to return, 1 to 3; omit for three. Three is what the grounding service answers per call, so a larger number is refused before the request is sent rather than returned as an error you cannot act on. Close-up previews are capped at the first six across a step: the request window holds 24 images and refuses rather than dropping the oldest. Breadth is not free: three regions cost roughly 479 milliseconds against 244 for one, so raise it from one when you are choosing between instances and leave it otherwise.

text.description: Short visible object or part description, never a simulator identifier.

arm.description: Arm whose wrist RGB-D joins head in scene fusion and whose source-bound ARX X5 end-effector compiler is used.

max_candidates.description: Maximum compiled candidates; omit for three.

target_ref.description: Current observation-bound target from grounding or segmentation; target-mask points remain tied to its source camera.

place_plan.description: Closed placement evidence request; no user-supplied release, stability, contact or success assertions.

arm.description: Required selected RoboDojo arm; uses this arm's measured public link6 pose and command history. The other arm is not moved or granted holding permission.

destination_boundary_ref.description: Current-observation target_ref selecting the visible functional opening — the rim for open_container, the front aperture or frame for front_cavity — or null when the destination has none. Required for those two kinds and refused for support_surface, each as a structured error naming this field rather than a schema branch. Dimensionless reference; a whole-container mask or its centroid does not establish cavity clearance.

destination_kind.description: Destination geometry family for this placement. support_surface places onto a visible supporting patch and has no opening. open_container places into an upward-open container and also requires destination_boundary_ref naming its visible rim. front_cavity places through a front aperture onto visible interior support and also requires destination_boundary_ref naming that aperture or frame. Dimensionless closed vocabulary; a whole-object mask or its centroid is not a functional region.

destination_support_ref.description: Current-observation target_ref selecting the visible supporting patch the object is placed on: the support patch itself for support_surface, the visible interior support for open_container and front_cavity. Dimensionless reference, not a coordinate. A hidden bottom cannot be inferred as evidence, and the parent object's mask is not the patch.

object_ref.description: Current-observation target_ref for the visible object being placed, from vision_segment or vision_ground; stale references are rejected. The selected mask is not semantic identity ground truth.

orientation_requirement.description: Select none when no orientation claim is needed, or upright when the selected object's visible rim normal must agree with world up. Without admissible rim points, upright evidence is unknown; no PCA object axis is invented.

phase.description: Request one next placement step: preplace alignment, lower approach, or a short post-release exit; not a complete execution script.

prior_assessment_ref.description: Immutable same-round assessment identifier for audit comparison only; never an executable motion handle.

protected_before_refs.description: Zero to three earlier same-round target_refs for protected visible regions, index-aligned with protected_current_refs: entry i is the earlier state of the region named by protected_current_refs[i]. Both arrays must have the same length or the call is refused with the shorter field named. Dimensionless references; future or cross-round references are rejected.

items.description: One earlier same-round target_ref for a protected visible region. Dimensionless reference, not a coordinate.

protected_current_refs.description: Zero to three current-observation target_refs selecting the regions intended to match protected_before_refs entry by entry, of the same length as it. Dimensionless references; the association stays the Agent's responsibility and is never authenticated identity.

items.description: One current-observation target_ref for a protected visible region. Dimensionless reference, not a coordinate.

rim.description: Optional manually selected visible circular rim on the object, bound to the object_ref source camera. Circle fitting measures this selected rim normal, not cup identity or a PCA axis.

camera.description: Camera that produced object_ref; the runtime rejects a different source camera.

points_uv.description: Six to twelve ordered points on the same visible circular rim in native RGB pixels; all must be inside the source image and admissible object region with valid depth.

items.description: One [u,v] pixel in top-left OpenCV coordinates.
Non-negative native-image pixel coordinate; image bounds are checked at invocation.

approach_side.description: World-frame direction toward the object, never toward an arm: top stands off above the target and travels down (world -Z), front stands off at -X travelling +X, back at +X travelling -X, left at +Y travelling -Y, right at -Y travelling +Y.

arm.description: Which arm is asked. This is independent of approach_side. "both" asks the identical poses of each arm in one read-only call and returns one candidate per arm per pose.

max_candidates.description: How many poses to synthesise at that one standoff position, differing only by jaw roll about the approach axis. Omitted means 3. With arm "both" the result holds twice this many candidates.

standoff_m.description: Distance in metres from the target's visible-surface centroid to the candidate link6 position, along approach_side. Omitted means 0.10 m. Values outside 0.02-0.30 m are refused.

target_ref.description: Segmented target from the current observation, as returned by vision_segment or vision_ground. The standoff is measured from this target's visible-surface centroid in metres; a reference bound to an earlier observation is refused as stale.

targets.description: Non-empty sparse robot recovery routes. Omitted arms receive no drive target. This never resets the episode, objects or evaluator state.

left.description: Left-arm recovery strategy: previous returns to the joint configuration measured when this arm's most recent admitted pose action started, whether or not it arrived, or the episode reset joints if none has run; home uses the RoboDojo episode reset joints. Recovery actions do not replace previous. Neither changes its gripper command.

right.description: Right-arm recovery strategy: previous returns to the joint configuration measured when this arm's most recent admitted pose action started, whether or not it arrived, or the episode reset joints if none has run; home uses the RoboDojo episode reset joints. Recovery actions do not replace previous. Neither changes its gripper command.
